This Opportunity

WSP has an exciting career opportunity for an Environmental Remediation Project Manager/Office Manager
to join our Rifle, CO
team. Scope of this role includes remedial design, field investigations, contaminated site management, data analysis and team oversight. This role will work closely with contaminated site portfolio leads and ensure the correct delivery of projects within the oil and gas industry, as well as overseeing the Rifle office on a day-to-day basis, overseeing staff and assisting with monitoring progress on contractor submittals, requests for Information, information bulletins, change/field Orders. This role would report to the North Mountain Site Investigation and Remediation (SIR) Service Line lead and be able to draw on expertise and resources in the SIR team throughout Colorado and the West.

Will have the opportunity to be involved in projects with our Earth & Environment Team and be a part of a growing organization that meets our client’s objectives and solves their challenges.

Are you looking for an exciting career opportunity where you can put your skills and talents to work with an established engineering consulting firm that values its employees’ enthusiasm and technical contributions? Do you enjoy managing projects and bringing in new projects? We encourage you to apply for this opportunity. We provide the atmosphere to allow individuals to grow their career. We’d love you to join our team of friendly, hard-working, dedicated and collaborative professionals. Our ideal candidate is seeking challenging work and is committed to quality.

Rifle, Colorado is a small town located on the beautiful Western Slope of Colorado, and centrally located 30 minutes west of Glenwood Springs; 1 hour northeast of Grand Junction, CO; 90 minutes northwest of Aspen, CO; 2 hours west of Breckenridge, CO and 3 hours west of Denver, CO.

Located directly on the Colorado River and near some of Colorado’s most popular tourist destinations, Rifle is the ideal location for adventure seekers. Residents enjoy skiing, fly fishing, hiking, camping, rafting, kayaking, and mountain biking all located right out your backdoor. Rifle Mountain Park (popular with rock climbers) is located 16 miles north of Rifle and Rifle Falls, Rifle Gap and Harvey Gap state parks are close by. There is access to BLM areas Hubbard Mesa Open Area, Rifle Arch and the Roan Plateau. The Rifle Creek Golf Course is 6 miles north of the center of Rifle.

Your Impact

Assist Senior Project Managers with their duties as necessary.
Coordinate weekly scheduling meetings.
Assist project Teams with multiple projects as requested.
Provide support to other staff on processes and requirements, monitor contract compliance, participate in the development of contracts.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Manage/oversee projects under the client’s Terms and Conditions which have been negotiated prior.
Support field staff collecting soil, groundwater and air samples for field and/or laboratory analyses.
Assisting and reviewing in the creation of detailed maps, lithologic logs and cross sections gathering, tabulating and analyzing data.
Preparing and reviewing proposals, cost estimates and technical reports for regulatory agencies submittal.
Oversee the team operating and maintaining field equipment and instrumentation.
Understand federal and state rules and regulations regarding environmental permitting compliance and remediation.
Provide senior-level expertise and technical guidance on complex regulatory projects.
Lead and mentor geologists, engineers and environmental scientists, guiding junior staff.
Prepare technical and Forms reports related for the Energy and Carbon Management Commission, Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission and Utah Department of Oil, Gas and Mining.
Takes projects from original discovery through final remediation.
Oversee various moderately-complex projects without the oversight of a Senior Project Manager and minimal oversight from technical teams.
Responsible for assembling project/task teams and assigning individual responsibilities, identifying appropriate resources needed. Given the complexity of the project, these teams could be larger, multi-disciplinary, and may reside in various states.
Develop the project scope and objectives, as well as clarify the role and function of each team member to effectively coordinate the activities of the team.
Identify, monitor, and mitigate risk on projects where the client may not have a full understanding of the project risks.
Take lead in development of proposals in collaboration with others.
Plan the execution of the project and monitor performance according to the project execution plan and the contract terms and conditions.
Manage project closure aspects ensuring correct project documentation.
Ensure project team (including sub-consultants/contractors) have understood and continually reassess the HSSE requirements of the project.
Develop and ensure adherence to the project schedule.
Supervise change request activities by appropriately addressing anticipated scope changes as they evolve and can advise others on scope change.
Assess and predict the possible impacts of schedule changes and the time management outcomes for future project impacts.
Develop a multi-disciplinary project budget and interact with subcontractors to develop the project budget.
Assign project budgets to task leaders and manage their performance.
Ensure compliance with client invoicing requirements and timely payment.
Will travel to project sites mostly in western Colorado and surrounding states. Approximately 10% overnight travel.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

BS degree in Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science, or related discipline; PG or PE license preferred.
Minimum of 7 -10+ years of environmental consulting and/or project management experience.
Demonstrated experience with project financial tracking, and change management related to scopes of work.CAD, Civil 3D®, ArcGIS experience a plus
Expertise in project planning, numerical tracking and analysis (e.g., using MS Excel or similar programs).
Highly organized, adaptable, a developing leader and calm under pressure.
Experience in managing multi-discipline teams.
Effective interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to a scientific and non-scientific audience.
Highly capable self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
Ability to work independently and provide guidance and leadership to junior team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
Proficiency with technical writing, office automation and communication software, technology, and tools.
Ability to assertively direct others in the field such as subcontracted drillers, excavation contractors, utility locators, and others to consistently complete tasks safely and efficiently.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek
Ability and willingness to travel to project sites mostly in western Colorado and surrounding states. Approximately 10% overnight travel.
Must pass drug test, background check and must have a satisfactory driving record in accordance with the Company's driving (MVR) policy.

Professional licensure/certification.
40-Hour OSHA Health & Safety Training (HAZWOPER) (29 CFR 1910.120) preferred.

jobs.title: Environmental Project Manager (Environmental Remediation) - Goshen, NY or Woodbridge, NJ
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is seeking an experienced Environmental Project Manager
to join our Environmental Investigation, and Remediation team in the Goshen, New York or Woodbridge, New Jersey area
.

This position is ideal for an environmental professional with a background in engineering, environmental science, geology, or a related technical discipline
who has strong technical and project management capabilities.

The successful candidate will manage environmental projects for private-sector industrial in northern New Jersey. We are particularly interested in candidates with strong technical backgrounds in soil assessment, groundwater fate and transport, non-aqueous phase liquids (NAPL), and environmental chemistry. In addition, candidates should have strong project management skills, including the ability to plan and manage the scope, schedule, and budget of multiple fast-paced environmental assessment and remediation projects.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Tetra Tech is a leader in the environmental industry, providing strategic planning, consulting, engineering, investigation, remediation, and compliance support for private-sector, industrial, and public-sector clients.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to lead projects addressing complex environmental challenges across multiple media, including soil, groundwater, sediment, surface water, and air
. You will work directly with clients, regulatory agencies, technical teams, and subcontractors to develop practical solutions and successfully deliver projects.

Position Summary

Working alongside a multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, geologists, designers, and technical specialists, you will manage environmental investigation, remediation, and related projects from initial scoping through completion.

The position will include responsibility for project scope, schedule, budget, technical quality, staffing, client communication, and financial performance
. Depending on the project, responsibilities may include interpreting federal, state, and local environmental regulations; directing site investigations and remediation activities; evaluating technical data and calculations; and overseeing preparation of reports, plans, cost estimates, permit applications, and other deliverables.

Much of the technical work may support the investigation and/or remediation of active and inactive NJDEP Site Remediation Program sites.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Manage environmental investigation, remediation, and related consulting projects.
Manage project planning, scope, schedules, budgets, staffing, subcontractors, deliverables, and financial performance.
Plan, develop, coordinate, and direct multidisciplinary project teams.
Interpret and apply applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Assess environmental conditions, potential impacts, regulatory requirements, and technical challenges.
Scope environmental investigations, remediation programs, compliance activities, and other technical projects.
Review and interpret site-specific technical data, calculations, laboratory results, reports, drawings, cost estimates, environmental permit applications, and permit terms and conditions.
Prepare and/or oversee preparation of technical reports, work plans, permit applications, specifications, cost estimates, and other project deliverables.
Provide technical leadership and sound professional judgment when addressing complex project issues.
Coordinate with regulatory agencies, clients, laboratories, subcontractors, and other project stakeholders.
Direct and review the work of engineers, scientists, geologists, field personnel, and other technical staff.
Maintain project quality through appropriate technical review and quality assurance/quality control procedures.
Collaborate with the senior technical team to develop site closure strategies.
Mentor and support the professional development of junior and mid-level staff.
Manage multiple projects, clients, deadlines, and priorities concurrently.
Prepare proposals, scopes of work, schedules, staffing plans, and cost estimates.
Participate in client meetings, presentations, and interviews.
Identify upcoming client needs and opportunities for additional work.
Conduct periodic field and site visits to support project delivery and maintain familiarity with project conditions.
Assist field team implementing planned projects.
Work at remediation sites, construction sites, and other locations where heavy equipment, contamination, or other environmental or physical hazards may be present.
Travel within northern New Jersey based on project and client needs.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geology, or a related environmental or technical discipline.
Minimum of 5 years of relevant environmental consulting experience, including experience in one or more of the following:
Environmental investigation and remediation.
Brownfield or contaminated site redevelopment.
Industrial or private-sector environmental consulting.
Demonstrated project management experience, including responsibility for project scope, budgets, schedules, staffing, and deliverables.
Experience communicating directly with clients and managing client expectations.
Working knowledge of applicable federal and state environmental regulations.
Experience managing or coordinating multidisciplinary technical teams.
Strong technical problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational and time-management skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities.
Self-motivated and disciplined, with the ability to learn new software and work effectively both independently and collaboratively.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build productive relationships with clients, colleagues, regulators, and subcontractors.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Project.
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to client and project sites as needed.
Possess or able to obtain a Transportation Worker Identification Card (TWIC) by hire date.

Preferred Qualifications

7–10+ years of environmental consulting experience with progressively increasing project and client management responsibility.
Professional Engineer (PE), Professional Geologist (PG), or other applicable professional certification or licensure.
Experience with New Jersey environmental regulations and regulatory programs.
Experience working with NJDEP.
Experience managing investigation and remediation projects involving soil, groundwater, sediment, vapor intrusion, or other environmental media.
Experience working with sites with intermingled contamination.
Experience supporting industrial and private-sector environmental clients.
Experience developing scopes, budgets, and fee estimates and managing project financial performance, including invoicing.
Demonstrated ability to mentor and develop junior technical staff.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate environmental assessment data and determine the next step in the remediation process.
Experience with Autodesk Civil 3D, GIS, or other relevant environmental or engineering software is a plus.

Physical Requirements

Regularly required to sit and work at a computer for extended periods, with occasional standing and walking within an office environment.
Occasionally required to lift or move up to 10 lbs., with infrequent lifting of up to 25 lbs.
Requires use of hands for typing, handling materials, and operating office and field equipment.
Vision abilities include close vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
May travel to field sites, generally approximately 10–30% of the time, depending on project and client needs.
Field assignments may involve walking on uneven terrain and working around active construction, remediation, landfill, or industrial operations.
When in the field, must be able to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including a respirator when required, and meet applicable medical clearance requirements.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those encountered while performing the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made.

Office-based work typically involves low hazard exposure, though noise levels may vary depending on nearby activities or equipment.
Outdoor project work may involve exposure to heat, cold, precipitation, uneven terrain, heavy equipment, physical hazards, and potential chemical or environmental hazards.
Appropriate PPE, including hearing protection and respiratory protection where applicable, may be required.
Travel between project sites, client locations, and Tetra Tech offices may be required, with employees expected to operate vehicles safely under varying weather, traffic, and environmental conditions.

Additional Information

This position will be based near Tetra Tech’s Goshen, New York or Woodbridge, New Jersey office.
A hybrid work arrangement may be available based on project, client, and team needs, with the expectation that the employee will be available for in-person client meetings, office collaboration, and project site visits as needed.
Regional travel throughout New York, New Jersey, and surrounding areas may be required.
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. Tetra Tech SWE will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work visa status for this opportunity (no sponsorship is available for H-1B, L-1, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, F-1, J-1, OPT, CPT or any other employment-based visa).

Pay:
$75,000 – 125,000 annually, commensurate with skill level, geography region and experience.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 30,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor, and we request priority referral of veterans.

We invite applications from all interested parties.

Explore our open positions at https://www.tetratech.com/careers. Follow us on social media to learn more about our people, culture, and opportunities:

Demonstrated record of drafting and negotiating Memoranda of Agreement or Programmatic Agreements to execution.
Direct, sustained consultation experience with multiple SHPOs and with THPOs or Tribal representatives.

Experience with ArcGIS Pro, geospatial analysis, archaeological predictive modeling, or cultural resources GIS applications.

50 % on average

Field experience in construction or environmental projects.
